fluff.overview: The Tempest is a sixty-five-ton heavy BattleMech designed by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited as a replacement for the aging Thunderbolt in Free Worlds League service. Originating in the late 3040s and relying on little advanced technology, the Clan Invasion and resulting research and development effort led to radical modifications, and the production model fielded in 3055 bore little resemblance to the initial concept. Irian BattleMechs Unlimited produces the Tempest at facilities on both Irian and Angell II, and the design has earned a reputation as a versatile and well-balanced heavy combatant that has proven difficult to improve upon. Combat operations have prompted the creation of several variants as both field modifications and factory-built options.
fluff.capabilities:
The Tempest's primary armament centers on a Zeus Slingshot Gauss rifle, delivering devastating long-range firepower without generating waste heat. A Sutel Precision Line large pulse laser supplements this at medium to long ranges, while three Diplan M3 medium lasers and an Irian Weapons Works 60mm SRM-6 rack provide punishing close-range firepower. The Gauss rifle carries two tons of ammunition for sixteen rounds of fire, and the SRM-6 has one ton of ammunition providing fifteen salvos.

The original design concept called for twin PPCs, but Irian designers replaced this configuration with the Gauss rifle and large pulse laser combination for the production model. Four Chilton 465 jump jets grant the Tempest a one hundred twenty meter jump capability, allowing it to keep pace with many lighter 'Mechs despite a mediocre cruising speed of forty-three kilometers per hour. Fine-tuning and testing on Irian's varied landscapes led the manufacturer to claim the Tempest operates across any terrain without loss of capability, an assertion the League military has tested on several occasions. Twelve tons of Maximillian 100 armor provide respectable protection for a sixty-five ton chassis, though the lack of CASE leaves the XL engine vulnerable to catastrophic ammunition explosions.
fluff.history:
The Tempest's origins trace to the late 3040s, when Irian BattleMechs Unlimited began developing a replacement for the venerable Thunderbolt in Free Worlds League service. The project initially used little advanced technology, but the shock of the Clan Invasion in 3049 prompted massive investment in research and development across the Inner Sphere. The Tempest design was radically overhauled to incorporate newly recovered Star League-era technologies, and the production TMP-3M that rolled off the Irian assembly line in 3055 was fundamentally different from the original prototype.

The Tempest's introduction immediately created friction within the Free Worlds League's defense industry. When Earthwerks attempted to market their updated TDR-9M Thunderbolt variant, Irian BattleMechs Unlimited lobbied the League Central Coordination and Command to halt new Thunderbolt production, arguing the Tempest rendered further Thunderbolt development unnecessary. The resulting corporate dispute was only resolved when the Word of Blake brokered a compromise, pitting the two designs against each other in a combat trial to determine which would supply the Blakist military.

Free Worlds military strategists embraced the Tempest, deploying it throughout the FWLM in formations that deliberately echoed Star League Defense Force doctrine. Lance- and company-sized Tempest units, often paired with the lighter Shadow Hawk, created flexible strike forces capable of rapid offensive and defensive operations. The largest concentrations served in the Marik Militias, Free Worlds Legions, and Fusiliers of Oriente. The design made its greatest impression in the Sirian Lancers, where its balance of firepower and agility proved vital during Operation Guerrero and the subsequent liberation of Sirius and Procyon.

The Jihad devastated the Tempest's production infrastructure. The Irian facility fell under Word of Blake control, and while production continued under Blakist oversight, many Free Worlds League units found themselves cut off from spare parts and replacement chassis. The establishment of the Angell II production line by Irian Technologies helped offset this loss, though the facility did not reach operational capacity until 3077. Following the Jihad, the Republic of the Sphere assumed control of both facilities, allegedly taking the Irian line offline during the 3090s, though production reportedly continued in secret.

The collapse of the Republic and the reformation of the Free Worlds League saw Irian BattleMechs Unlimited regain control of its production lines. Regarded as a difficult design to improve upon, it took until the 3130s for a formal successor variant to debut. New variants including the TMP-4M and the Clan Protectorate-backed Tempest C emerged during the Dark Age, demonstrating the design's continued relevance more than eight decades after its introduction.
fluff.deployment: Produced under the auspices of the Clan Protectorate, the Tempest C melds the proven Inner Sphere chassis and armor with a mix of Inner Sphere and Clan-specification weaponry. A Clan-grade large pulse laser and Gauss rifle replace their Inner Sphere counterparts in the arm mounts, while three standard medium lasers are retained. An ATM-9 launcher mounted in the left torso provides tactical flexibility through its variable ammunition types, though only two tons of ammunition somewhat limit this advantage. As with all previous Tempest designs, no CASE has been fitted, a persistent vulnerability that Clan warriors have noted with some disapproval.
